hypothesis: Learning nonlinear features from raw real-valued sensor/action pairs, and applying fast within-world linear adaptation to those learned features, improves unfamiliar switched-world counterfactual prediction beyond the same untrained random features and independently calibrated nonparametric RBF kernel ridge. No analytic nonlinear basis given to any S17 candidate or KRR control.

arms.type: trainable 2→32→12 tanh MLP on raw state/action, 12-dim ridge adaptive coefficients per world; same initial MLP as random
identical initial MLP but never trained; same ridge coefficient adaptation
strong conventional RBF kernel ridge over raw (x,u); gamma, decay, regularization CALIBRATION-ONLY
32-unit GRU on raw 4-channel continuous history with query-conditioned 3-channel 32-unit MLP future-derivative head
evaluator uses hidden world parameters only to generate ground-truth targets
negative context swap for learned feature and RBF predictors

world.generator: reuse S16 world() function byte-identically, with NO S16 analytic basis() or consequence() accessible to learned-feature, random-feature, kernel or GRU predictors. Evaluator knows true nonlinear law.
world.nonlinear_family: xnext=x+dt*(-a*x+b*u+c*tanh(2*x)+d*x*u), unknown to all S17 candidate models
world.unseen_function_split: xnext uses tanh(3*x) after switch, unknown to candidates; OOD parameter ranges as S16
world.physics_bias_disclosure: Estimator model uses the known Euler residual (xnext-x)/dt and supervised counterfactual target, so it has a discrete-time numerical dynamics prior, but no correct nonlinear feature formula.

calibration.tie_breaker: argmin mean calibration MSE then smaller gamma then larger decay then larger ridge; never use test splits to select

classifications.report_gru: Independent trained GRU comparator metrics, not a combined success label
classifications.no_claim: No proof of token-free general intelligence, learned unknown causal laws, true analog hardware or novel algorithm. These are raw numeric time samples; feature-ridge and Gaussian-kernel methods are established.
